candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: maintain aseptic/sterile technique and reduce infection risk during nursing procedures
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — sterile-field maintenance
candidate.educational_objective: Maintain sterile technique by recognizing the outer 1-inch border of a sterile field as contaminated.

options.A: As contaminated; sterile items should be kept away from this border
options.B: As the preferred area for placing sterile instruments
options.C: As sterile only when the drape remains dry
options.D: As sterile once the nurse has donned sterile gloves

candidate.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills identifies any part of a sterile field within 1 inch of the edge as contaminated. Sterile supplies should therefore be kept away from that border. Dryness or the nurse's use of sterile gloves does not convert the 1-inch edge into a sterile area. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The area within 1 inch of the edge of a sterile field is considered contaminated and should not be used for sterile items.
candidate.source_locator: Chapter 4, Sterile Fields / establishing and maintaining a sterile field: areas considered contaminated include any part of the field within 1 inch from the edge
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
candidate.stem: While maintaining a sterile field, how should the nurse treat the outer 1-inch border of the field?
